newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica, First Chicago report higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica, First Chicago report higher earnings.

text.p: More big banks reported strong fourth quarter earnings Wednesday, buoyed by solid loan growth and despite growing problems in the lucrative credit card business.

BankAmerica Corp., the nation's third-largest bank, said earnings rose 6 percent in the quarter, First Chicago NBD Corp.'s profits jumped 19 percent, Fleet Financial Group Inc. said income grew 16 percent, and Wachovia Corp.'s earnings rose 17 percent.
Republic New York Corp.'s profits grew 16 percent and PNC Bank Corp. reported a profit compared with a loss in the 1995 quarter.
Analysts said the quarter was strong with the sole blemish a rise in credit card losses at some banks, though the card business overall remained profitable at most institutions.
They said stock buybacks boosted per share results at some banks, and that several bank stocks rose in a down day on Wall Street.
"Clearly the credit card losses have continued to creep up," said Michael Mayo at Lehman Bros., adding that profits overall continued the "steady upward progress" banks have made in recent years.

San Francisco-based BankAmerica said it earned $747 million in the quarter, up from $704 million in the 1995 quarter. Earnings per share of $1.93, up from $1.74, came in better than analysts' estimates of $1.90 a share and BankAmerica stock jumped $5.625 to close at $107.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Chief Financial Officer Michael O'Neill told reporters that the company's domestic loans grew by $3 billion to $139 billion during the quarter, with loans in California accounting for about 30 percent of the gain.
For the year, BankAmerica earned $2.9 billion, or $7.31 a share, up from $2.7 billion, or $6.49 a share, in 1995.
First Chicago, the nation's ninth largest banking company with assets of $104.6 billion, said it earned $377 million in the fourth quarter, up from $318 million in the 1995 period.
The Chicago-based company, which owns First National Bank of Chicago and other banks in Indiana and Florida, said it earned $1.14 a share, up from 96 cents a share a year earlier.
For the year, First Chicago earned a record $1.44 billion, or $4.32 a share, up from $1.34 billion, or $3.99 a share.

"Our record earnings exemplify the successful first year of First Chicago NBD," said Chairman Verne Istock. "We met all of our merger-related goals on or ahead of schedule." First Chicago Corp. completed its merger with NBD Bancorp Inc. on Dec, 1, 1995.
First Chicago stock rose 87.5 cents to $55, also on the NYSE.
Fleet Financial, the nation's 11th largest bank, said it earned $302 million, or $1.05 a share, up from $260 million, or 94 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.
The stock of Boston-based Fleet fell 62.5 cents to $51.625 on the NYSE.
Pittsburgh-based PNC, the No. 13 bank, said it earned $271.9 million, or 80 cents a share, compared with a loss of $176.2 million, or 52 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter.
PNC stock fell 37.5 cents to $38.375 on the NYSE.
Republic, the 17th biggest bank, reported earnings of $100.6 million, or $1.82 a share, up from $86.8 million, or $1.54 a share, in the 1995 period.
Republic New York stock rose 25 cents to $83.625 on the NYSE.
No. 20 bank Wachovia Corp. said it earned $171 million, or $1.02 a share, in the quarter, up from $146.2 million, or 85 cents a share, in the year-earlier period.

Gains reflected increases in net interest income and lower expenses, said L. M. Baker Jr., chief executive officer of the Winston-Salem, N.C.-based company, with operations in the Carolinas and Georgia.
Its stock lost 50 cents to $56.375, also on the NYSE.
